Architecture Diagram

The repository contains an ASP.NET MVC job-search website and a separate console utility that loads sample data into Azure Search. The website reads job and ZIP-code indexes; the loader creates and populates those indexes from repository data files.

Data Storage & External Services

There is no relational database or local persistence layer. The website queries the nycjobs and zipcodes Azure Search indexes; the console utility reads schemas and sample JSON files from the repository and writes index definitions and documents to Azure Search. The website also loads the Bing Maps JavaScript API in the browser.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The MVC website keeps search orchestration in JobsSearch, while the separate loader performs index administration and bulk import.
  • Azure Search is the system of record for searchable documents; local JSON files provide sample import data.
  • The UI and backend use JSON over synchronous HTTP requests; no message broker or service-discovery mechanism is present.

DTOs & Contracts

NYCJob is the search response wrapper containing result documents, facets, and a count. NYCJobLookup wraps one Azure Search SearchDocument for the detail view. These are mutable C# classes; no explicit OpenAPI document, protobuf, GraphQL schema, or custom API serializer configuration was found. Azure Search SDK model types supply the indexed document contract.

Communication Patterns

  • Browser-to-website requests use synchronous HTTP form posts for search and lookup, and an HTTP GET for suggestions.
  • JobsSearch uses the Azure Search .NET client synchronously for search, suggestion, document lookup, and ZIP-code search.
  • The loader sends synchronous REST requests to Azure Search with HttpClient; JSON payloads are used to create indexes and upload documents.
  • No message queue, retry policy, circuit breaker, service discovery, API gateway, or client-side load balancing was found.
  • Azure Search calls use an API key. No application-level authentication or authorization is configured for the MVC actions, and the repository does not show HTTPS enforcement for the website.

Core Business Workflows

The application helps users find and inspect sample New York City job postings. Users can search and filter postings, explore results by location, and open an individual job record; a separate utility maintains the sample search indexes.

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
NYCJobsWebJob Search and Location SearchNo database-owned entities; reads indexed job and ZIP-code documentsAzure Cognitive Search
AzureSearchBackupRestoreSample Index MaintenanceCreates and populates job and ZIP-code indexesAzure Cognitive Search; local schema and JSON files

The website is the read/query interface. The loader is the only component shown modifying the search indexes; there is no service-to-service domain exchange beyond the shared search service.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Search and Refine Job Postings

  1. The browser submits the search text, selected facets, sort mode, page, and location values to the MVC search action.
  2. If the query is blank, the application treats it as a wildcard search. If a positive distance is selected, the application searches the ZIP-code index to obtain a center point.
  3. JobsSearch constructs Azure Search options, including a result limit, facets, filters, and selected ordering, then queries the job index.
  4. The controller returns the results, facets, and total count as JSON. The browser refreshes result cards, counts, filters, paging, and map markers.

Workflow 2: Inspect a Job Posting

  1. A user selects a result and the browser requests the job-details page.
  2. The page submits the selected document ID to the lookup action.
  3. JobsSearch retrieves the document from the job index and the controller returns it as JSON for display.

Workflow 3: Load Sample Index Data

  1. The operator runs the console loader with Azure Search target settings.
  2. For each of the zipcodes and nycjobs indexes, the loader attempts to delete the existing index, posts the schema, and uploads matching local JSON files.
  3. The loader prints request errors to the console; no rollback, retry, or transaction spanning the index operations is implemented.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There is no API gateway or multi-service aggregation. The web application obtains job and ZIP-code data from separate Azure Search indexes. A distance-filtered query first resolves the ZIP code to a geographic point, then passes that point to the job-index search. The index loader writes both indexes from local sample data; no message or event synchronizes changes.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant User participant Browser participant MVC as "NYCJobsWeb" participant Logic as "JobsSearch" participant Search as "Azure Search" User->>Browser: Enter terms and choose filters Browser->>MVC: Submit search criteria MVC->>MVC: Use wildcard when search text is blank opt Distance filter selected MVC->>Logic: Resolve ZIP-code location Logic->>Search: Search ZIP-code index Search-->>Logic: Coordinates end MVC->>Logic: Search job postings Logic->>Search: Apply text, facet, salary, sort, and distance criteria Search-->>Logic: Documents, facets, and count Logic-->>MVC: Search response MVC-->>Browser: JSON search result Browser-->>User: Display jobs and map markers User->>Browser: Select a job Browser->>MVC: Request job details by document id MVC->>Logic: Retrieve indexed document Logic->>Search: Look up job document Search-->>Logic: Job document Logic-->>MVC: Lookup response MVC-->>Browser: JSON job details Browser-->>User: Display posting

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A blank search string becomes *, which searches all available job documents.
  • A positive distance invokes ZIP-code lookup and adds a geographic-distance condition to the job query.
  • Business-title and posting-type values are applied as facets/filters; a salary facet selects a 50,000-unit range.
  • Sorting supports featured relevance, ascending or descending salary, and most recent posting.
  • The search requests a page size of 10. The loader refreshes indexes by deleting and recreating them before upload.
  • Search and REST exceptions are caught and written to console output; there is no business-level retry, compensation, audit trail, or transaction across multiple index operations.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The projects target .NET Framework 4.7.2 and 4.5, respectively, and use older MVC and browser-library versions. Dependency scanning identified high-severity CVE-2024-21907 in both declared Newtonsoft.Json versions and critical CVE-2021-26701 in System.Text.Encodings.Web 4.6.0. Package compatibility for a net10.0 migration needs a project-format-aware assessment; the current legacy projects cannot be fully analyzed by AppCAT in this Linux environment.

Notable Observations

  • Newtonsoft.Json is declared at different versions in the website and loader.
  • packages.config dependency resolution is unavailable through dotnet list package; the inventory therefore lists declared packages only.
  • No test-scoped NuGet dependencies or test project were detected.

Caching Strategy

No application cache, cache provider, TTL, or cache-aside behavior was identified. Azure Search client instances are held in static fields in the web application, but search results are not cached by application code.

Data Ownership Boundaries

Both the website and loader access the same externally managed Azure Search service. The website reads index data; the loader owns the operational workflow that deletes/recreates indexes and uploads documents from local JSON files. There is no cross-service database access or separate read/write store.
